```python
def put(self, key, value):
    if key in self.data:  # If key already exists in cache
        self.order.remove(key)  # Remove from order (move to end)
    elif len(self.data) >= self.capacity:  # If capacity reached
        oldest = self.order.pop(0)  # Remove first element from order
        del self.data[oldest]  # Delete from data
    self.data[key] = value  # Add key-value pair
    self.order.append(key)  # Append to order
```

When a key is already in the cache, `self.order.remove(key)` removes it and then `self.order.append(key)` appends it to the end. So the key gets moved to the back of the order list! This means keys that have been accessed recently stay at the end, which makes them eligible for eviction later.
